header:
Date: 2025-12-16
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (CTO, Nimbus Health), Mark Liu (Eng Lead), Elena Torres (DevOps), Hannah Kim (PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning for Nimbus Health pilot. Discussed canary strategy, cutover rehearsal, monitoring/alerts, runbooks, and outstanding infra items (VPC peering, test creds). Agreed on action items and dates for final benchmarks and rehearsal.
topics: Benchmarks: latency, cost, KV cache behavior
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, quick roll call.
[00:06] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here.
[00:08] Mark Liu: Mark.
[00:10] Elena Torres: Elena.
[00:12] Alex Chen: Great. So agenda today is the rollout and go-live planning for the pilot, make sure we have canary, cutover, monitoring and runbooks lined up. Samira, do you want to start with the canary proposal?
[00:23] Samira Patel: Yeah thanks, so our recommended canary is a two-phase ramp. Phase one 5% traffic for 24 hours, validate latency and error rate and key QA prompts, phase two 25% for 48 hours then full cutover if everything looks green. We'll rely on per-route SLOs, token-cost monitors, and a small set of smoke tests that run against the cached prefixes.
[00:44] Mark Liu: Quick Q — when you say "cached prefixes" do you mean the KV cache? We saw some noise in the cache hit rate during the last benchmark.
[00:50] Samira Patel: Yes, KV cache. We recommend enabling prefix caching for the top-10 prompts. That should reduce token cost by like ~20-30% for those flows, but we need to test with your real traffic pattern because you have a lot of long-context clinical notes which changes hit dynamics.
[01:10] Priya Rao: Right don't want to overoptimize just for short prompts. Also data residency — reminder that some patient metadata needs to stay in-region. We still plan private VPC deployment, right?
[01:20] Alex Chen: Correct, Private deployment with VPC peering in your us-west-2 region. We'll use customer-managed KMS for keys. Elena, is networking ready for peering?
[01:28] Elena Torres: Almost. We need one more temporary test credential and the peering route table entry. I'll create those today but we need Redwood to confirm IP ranges.
[01:36] Alex Chen: I'll follow up offline with the IP ranges.
[01:38] Hannah Kim: For the canary, what's our rollback criteria? If latency jumps or model quality regresses, what's the threshold?
[01:44] Samira Patel: Good Q. Proposed thresholds: 95th percentile latency increase >20% over baseline OR error rate >1% absolute OR any quality regression flagged by your eval suite on the top-20 prompts. If hit, automatic rollback to previous model variant and route all traffic back. We'll include that in the runbook.
[02:03] Mark Liu: The 20% latency seems tight; our baseline is already near the threshold for UI SLOs. Can we do lower for the first phase?
[02:10] Samira Patel: We can tighten to 10% for phase one (5% traffic) and relax to 20% for phase two. That gives you safer initial guardrails.
[02:18] Priya Rao: Sounds reasonable.
[02:20] Alex Chen: Let's talk monitoring — Jordan can you run through the dashboard and alert hooks?
[02:25] Jordan Reyes: Sure. We'll provide a per-route dashboard showing p50/p95/p99 latency, token consumption, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, error rates, and model version distribution. Alerts: p95 > threshold, error rate spike, and quality regression webhook. We'll give SREs read access and can set up a PagerDuty integration for critical alerts.
[02:44] Elena Torres: PagerDuty yes, we need CS on-call to own the first-level. Also need audit logs for every model version switch for compliance.
[02:51] Samira Patel: Audit logs are available — we'll surface deployment events and API keys usage. We'll also provide a signed SOC2 checklist doc.
[02:58] Priya Rao: Good. On runbooks — who does what during cutover? Need clear owners, timer, rollback steps.
[03:05] Samira Patel: Runbook draft: pre-checks (VPC, KMS, creds), smoke tests (10 critical prompts), start canary (route 5%), monitor for 24h, if green ramp to 25% for 48h, final cutover. Owners: Nimbus SREs own infra checks, Redwood SE owns smoke tests and live metrics, AE owns stakeholder comms. We'll include explicit API commands to change routing and model pin.
[03:31] Hannah Kim: Would like a rehearsal. Can we do a dry-run with synthetic traffic?
[03:35] Alex Chen: Yes, we suggest a 2-hour rehearsal with a staged ramp, execute rollback, and validate oncall procedures. Proposed date 2025-12-20.
[03:44] Priya Rao: That works for execs. We need the rehearsal to include the incident comms playbook.
[03:49] Jordan Reyes: We'll draft the incident comms template.
[03:52] Mark Liu: Benchmarks — last time Redwood ran local perf we saw a p95 of 600ms with quantized model; with our long contexts it jumped. Can you rerun with the KV cache and a 512-token test?
[04:03] Samira Patel: Yes we'll run a 5k-request benchmark with your traffic pattern, KV cache enabled, and token length distribution you provide. Expect results by 2025-12-17. Note transcription: sometimes model names get mangled in the notes, but we'll call it "rvx-quant" internally for the test.
[04:21] Elena Torres: Security question: will Redwood’s private control plane see PHI in logs? We need to limit what leaves the VPC.
[04:28] Alex Chen: No PHI will be retained outside — logs are redacted, and you can opt into on-prem control plane where logs stay in your network. We'll document retention.
[04:36] Priya Rao: Good. Also procurement — legal wants an SLA addendum for the Dedicated nodes. Is that ready?
[04:42] Jordan Reyes: We have a draft SLA addendum; Alex will share with procurement after the rehearsal.
[04:48] Alex Chen: OK actions recap coming up. Any other concerns?
[04:51] Mark Liu: One more — A/B test for prompt variants during canary, how does Redwood support running two prompt templates simultaneously?
[04:58] Samira Patel: We support route-level A/B — you can split incoming traffic between model variants or prompt templates and we collect metrics per bucket. We'll include the A/B configuration in the runbook.
[05:10] Hannah Kim: Great. I just want to confirm who gets the monitoring access.
[05:13] Jordan Reyes: Nimbus SREs (Elena, Mark) will get admin-ish read; product and PM will get dashboard read-only. We'll add Hannah and Priya.
[05:22] Priya Rao: OK, thanks. If we get the runbook and benchmarks by end of week, we can do the rehearsal on the 20th.
[05:29] Alex Chen: Perfect. We'll send a calendar invite.
[05:31] Jordan Reyes: I'll also share the draft runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/nimbus-canary (note: internal link).
[05:39] Elena Torres: I'll open the peering ticket after the call.
[05:42] Alex Chen: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the action list.
[05:45] End of recording.
